header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #81 in AlexITC/expense-tracker: make pages URL friendly so selected filters live in the URL, starting with the bank statements account/status filter, and document the pattern. Full spec follows.

## Problem

Page state that the user selects is not reflected in the URL, so pages are not refreshable or shareable, and navigating back loses context.

Concrete case on the bank statements page (`web/.../pages/bankstatements/BankStatementsPage.scala`): selecting an account (the account filter) lives only in component state. Refreshing the page loses the selection, and going from a statement review back to the list does not restore the account that was selected. It resets to the default.

## Goal

Make selected filters and view state live in the URL.

- Selecting a bank statement account updates the URL (query param, e.g. `?account=<key>`), so a refresh restores the same account and the URL is shareable.
- Returning from a statement review to the list keeps the same account selected. The back navigation lands on the list with its prior filter intact.
- Deep links resolve on a cold load (this overlaps with the ctrl+click bug in #80, where opening `/bank-statements/{id}` in a new tab lands on the default page instead of the statement).

## Pattern to document

This is a general rule, not a one-off. Add it to the frontend guide (`docs/guide/frontend.md`): **pages must be URL friendly. User-selected filters and view selections go in the URL (path or query params), not only in component state, so pages are refreshable, shareable, and back-navigable.** Read initial state from the URL on mount; write to the URL on change (replace vs push chosen so the browser back button behaves sensibly).

## Scope

- Phase 1: the bank statements account filter, plus any other filters already on that page (statement status filter).
- Document the pattern so new pages follow it.
- Apply it to other filtered pages as a follow-up rather than all at once.
